plan.title: Vocabulary, architecture and event design
plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Before any engine code, the product gets its words, its map and its event design. This stage names every noun once, as an entry and as a schema, draws the Chopin-like plan room, and settles where the agent's work runs, so every later agent says the same things.
plan.current: cp-01 deploys both Workers from main with a version label and a rollback; migrations run by hand. There are no domain words yet: no schema package, no vocabulary, and an architecture doc that covers only two Workers and D1.
discoveries: The check reads every `Not:` line in `docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md` and scans exported names and command or event fields under `packages/schema` and `packages/domain`.
A banned word used only as a plain `Schema.Struct` key passes the check today; as an export, or inside `defineEvent` fields, it fails.
`bun scripts/arch.ts --coverage` blocks `packages/schema` until "Where it lives" names it, so the map changes with the package.
A sign-in is never called a session: in this product, a Session is where Participants ask the agent.
plan.endState: `just domain-vocabulary-check` passes, and fails when a banned word such as `Verdict` is exported. The architecture map and the agent-loop decision report open in the browser and show the plan room design.
notDoing: The engine or any decider; cp-03 builds the engine, later stages the Thread and Session.
Routes or pages; the API and the web app stay as cp-01 left them.
Renaming Session to Thread for the agent; that waits until after the workshop.
Workspace words such as repo, branch or preview; nothing uses them yet.
plan.approach: Words first, because every later name comes from them. Then the map, which places those words. Then the event design, and the one decision it depends on.

contexts.name: Planning
contexts.about: The words people write and decide with: a plan, its blocks, the threads on them.

contexts.name: Working together
contexts.about: Who is in a plan room. A person and the agent act alike.

contexts.name: Agent work
contexts.about: Asking the agent inside a plan: the sessions, and the runs in them.

contexts.name: Identity
contexts.about: Who can sign in, and on which device. Named here, built in cp-03.

vocabulary.meaning: A document tied to one repo; everything that happens to it is one stream, held by one PlanRoom.
One unit of a Plan: prose, an artifact or research. Last writer wins per block.
A comment thread anchored to one Block. Opens, collects Replies, ends in a Decision, once.
A message a Participant appends to an open Thread.
How a Thread ended: who decided, when, what, and the Block it changed. Stays attached to that Block.
An agent thread implementing one option and reporting back; a Decision chooses one.
An interactive page the agent built, embedded in a Block: a decision report, a state explorer.
A person or the agent in a plan room. Same commands, same rights; each command carries `by`.
Where Participants ask the agent inside one Plan. One stream each; only its starter ends it.
One Ask, from queued to its result. One at a time per Session; any Participant can steer it.
How a Participant signs in: email, name, password hash, admin or not. One stream per email.
One live sign-in on one device: a token's hash and when it expires.

spec.question: Where do a plan's comments and its sessions with the agent live?
spec.diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["You · plan on the left, sessions on the right"]
  AG["Agent · a participant like you"]
  A["API"]
  R[("Plan room · one per plan")]
  T["Threads · comments on blocks"]
  S["Sessions · asking the agent"]
  P -- "writes, replies, asks" --> A
  AG -- "same steps" --> A
  A -- "records it" --> R
  R -- "holds" --> T
  R -- "holds" --> S

steps.caption: You write in the plan on the left and ask the agent on the right.
Every change goes to the one plan room that holds this plan.
The room keeps both streams: threads on blocks, and sessions with the agent.
The agent signs in and goes through the same steps you do.

spec.question: What happens to one command, from a Participant to the read model?
spec.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Participant
  participant R as Plan room
  participant D as decide
  participant L as Event log
  participant V as Projection
  P->>R: ResolveThread thread-7, wrapper
  R->>L: read the thread's stream
  R->>D: state and command
  D-->>R: ThreadResolved, DecisionRecorded
  R->>L: append at the version it read
  L->>V: decisions row, same transaction

steps.caption: A Participant sends a command, an imperative in the vocabulary's words.
The room reads that aggregate's stream and folds it into state.
Only decide holds rules; it returns events in the past tense, or a rejection.
The events are appended against the version read, so a race decides again.
Projections are written in the same transaction, never behind the log.

decisions.question: Where should the agent's work run?

options.label: In the plan room, on Cloudflare

decisions.why: Only the plan room keeps working when the laptop closes, resumes after a crash, and lets two people ask in one place. It wakes a container only to run code.

viz.question: Where should the agent's work run?

axes.label: Cost while nobody is using it

options.label: In the browser tab
options.summary: The tab runs the agent beside you; nothing else to deploy.
options.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Y["You"]
  B["Browser tab · the agent runs here"]
  M["Model"]
  L["Work stops, nothing saved"]
  Y -- "ask" --> B
  B -- "think" --> M
  B -. "close the tab" .-> L

options.label: In the plan room, on Cloudflare
options.summary: A Durable Object per plan runs the agent and saves every step.
options.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Y["You and teammates"]
  R["Plan room · the agent runs here"]
  M["Model"]
  S[("Room storage · every step")]
  C["Container · only to run code"]
  Y -- "ask" --> R
  R -- "think" --> M
  R -- "saves" --> S
  R -- "run tests" --> C
  R -. "shows each step" .-> Y

tried.summary: sessions and runs saved in the room's own SQLite; every step reaches open tabs live

options.label: In a container
options.summary: One machine runs the agent and the code together.
options.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Y["You"]
  C["Container · the agent and the code"]
  M["Model"]
  D[("Its own disk")]
  G["Disk wiped when it stops"]
  Y -- "ask" --> C
  C -- "think" --> M
  C -- "saves" --> D
  C -. "stopped when idle" .-> G

steps.caption: You ask, and the tab runs the agent right next to you.
Close the laptop and the work stops; nothing was saved.
You and teammates ask in the same plan room.
The room saves every step, so a crash resumes where it stopped.
It wakes a container only to run code, then lets it sleep.
Everyone in the room sees each step as it happens.
The agent and the code share one machine, which is simple.
To save money it stops when idle, and its disk goes with it.

phases.name: Name it: the vocabulary and its schemas
phases.goal: Every noun has an entry with its banned synonyms and a schema in `packages/schema`. The vocabulary check passes, and fails on a banned word.

changes.intent: Four contexts; each entry names its schema, events, commands, and the words not to use.

contract.code:
## Context: Planning

### Decision
How a Thread ended: who decided, when, what was chosen, and the Block it changed.
Carried by: `Decision` schema · Events: `DecisionRecorded` · Commands: `ResolveThread`
Not: resolution, verdict, outcome, choice, conclusion

changes.intent: The vocabulary as Effect Schema types; no noun in code that is not here.
`@greenhouse/schema`, depending on `effect` and nothing else.
Fails on a command or event without an entry, or a banned identifier.

contract.code:
# check-domain-vocabulary.sh docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md packages [apps …]
# scans packages/schema and packages/domain (.ts, .tsx; not tests, *.d.ts, *.gen.ts, kernel.ts)
# ✗ <Name> is declared in code but no domain vocabulary entry lists it
# ✗ banned synonym '<word>' used as a domain identifier: <file:line>
# ✓ domain vocabulary and domain code agree (N names checked)   → exit 0

changes.intent: `domain-vocabulary-check` runs the script over `packages` and `apps`.
Name `packages/schema` under "Rules and shared words" in "Where it lives".

manual.text: Export `Verdict` from `packages/schema`; the check fails and names the line.

phases.name: Draw it: the plan room, the product, the design
phases.goal: The map shows the Chopin-like product: a plan with threads on its blocks, a sessions panel, one PlanRoom per plan, the agent as a Participant.

changes.intent: Map, walkthrough, "Where it lives" and "Allowed edges" for the plan room and the agent.

contract.code:
| Part of the map | Folders |
|---|---|
| Web app | `apps/web` |
| API | `apps/api` |
| Plan room | `apps/api` (the PlanRoom Durable Object), `packages/domain`, `packages/engine` |
| Rules and shared words | `packages/domain`, `packages/schema`, `docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md` |
| Settings, accounts and summaries | `apps/api/migrations`, `packages/db`, `packages/engine` |
| Agent | `packages/agent` |

changes.intent: Who uses Greenhouse, the job it does, and what it will not become.
The plan page: plan with threads on the left, sessions on the right.

manual.text: Step through `docs/architecture/index.html`; the agent goes through the same API.

phases.name: Model it: commands, events, streams
phases.goal: The event design is written down, one stream per aggregate, and the decision on where the agent's work runs is built and chosen.

changes.intent: An "Event design" section: commands go through decide, events are facts, projections fold them.

contract.code:
| Aggregate | Stream | Commands | Events |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thread | the plan's events for one thread | OpenThread, Reply, ResolveThread | ThreadOpened, ReplyPosted, ThreadResolved, DecisionRecorded |

| Account | `account-<email>`, in D1 | SignUp, OpenAccount, SignIn, SignOut | AccountOpened, SignedIn, SignedOut |

plan.title: Vocabulary, architecture and event design
plan.author: pratos with Claude Code
plan.summary: Before any engine code, the product gets its words, its map and its event design. This stage names every noun once, as an entry and as a schema, draws the Chopin-like plan room, and settles where the agent's work runs, so every later agent says the same things.
plan.current: cp-01 deploys both Workers from main with a version label and a rollback; migrations run by hand. There are no domain words yet: no schema package, no vocabulary, and an architecture doc that covers only two Workers and D1.
discoveries: The check reads every `Not:` line in `docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md` and scans exported names and command or event fields under `packages/schema` and `packages/domain`.
A banned word used only as a plain `Schema.Struct` key passes the check today; as an export, or inside `defineEvent` fields, it fails.
`bun scripts/arch.ts --coverage` blocks `packages/schema` until "Where it lives" names it, so the map changes with the package.
A sign-in is never called a session: in this product, a Session is where Participants ask the agent.
plan.endState: `just domain-vocabulary-check` passes, and fails when a banned word such as `Verdict` is exported. The architecture map and the agent-loop decision report open in the browser and show the plan room design.
notDoing: The engine or any decider; cp-03 builds the engine, later stages the Thread and Session.
Routes or pages; the API and the web app stay as cp-01 left them.
Renaming Session to Thread for the agent; that waits until after the workshop.
Workspace words such as repo, branch or preview; nothing uses them yet.
plan.approach: Words first, because every later name comes from them. Then the map, which places those words. Then the event design, and the one decision it depends on.
